title: If this, then that

## A branch is a choice

A branch is a choice the program makes after it asks a question. `if score >= 50:` picks one path when the comparison is true. The other path is `else`. The test uses comparison (`>=`), not assignment (`=`). Only one of those paths should run for a given score.

This bites when you print `"fail"` for every score, or when you write `if score = 50` and Python refuses to run. A score of `72` is already a pass, so a one-path script that always fails is lying about the data you were given. The number is sitting right there; the `if` has to look at it.

```python
score = 72
if score >= 50:
    print("pass")
else:
    print("fail")
```

A common mistake is mixing `=` into the test, or printing a canned word without looking at `score`. The exercise asks you to print `pass` when `score` is at least `50` (it is `72`), and to use a real `if` so the choice comes from the comparison.

description: A decision picks one path when a check is true.
